sanskrit: dhāraṇād dharmam ity āhur dharmo dhārayati prajāḥ yaḥ syād dhāraṇasaṃyuktaḥ sa dharma iti niścayaḥ
english: From its upholding, they say, dharma takes its name, for dharma upholds all creatures. Whatever is bound up with upholding — that, it is determined, is dharma.

sanskrit: ye 'nyāyena jihīrṣanto janā icchanti karhi cit akūjanena cen mokṣo nātra kūjet kathaṃ cana
english: When men, wishing to seize what is not theirs by right, demand something, then if release can be had by saying nothing, one should by no means speak out at all.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ kūjitavyaṃ vā śaṅkeran vāpy akūjataḥ śreyas tatrānṛtaṃ vaktuṃ satyād iti vicāritam
english: But where one must needs speak, or where silence itself would breed suspicion — there, it is reasoned, to utter a falsehood is better than the truth.

sanskrit: prāṇātyaye vivāhe vā sarvajñātidhanakṣaye narmaṇy abhipravṛtte vā pravaktavyaṃ mṛṣā bhavet adharmaṃ nātra paśyanti dharmatattvārthadarśinaḥ
english: In peril of life, or at a marriage, or to save all one's kinsmen and wealth, or in the course of jesting, a falsehood may be spoken — and in this those who see into the true meaning of dharma perceive no wrong.

sanskrit: yaḥ stenaiḥ saha saṃbandhān mucyate śapathair api śreyas tatrānṛtaṃ vaktuṃ tat satyam avicāritam
english: He who is freed of dealings with thieves even by means of oaths — for him to speak falsely there is the better course, and that, beyond all reasoning, is the truth.

sanskrit: na ca tebhyo dhanaṃ deyaṃ śakye sati kathaṃ cana pāpebhyo hi dhanaṃ dattaṃ dātāram api pīḍayet tasmād dharmārtham anṛtam uktvā nānṛtavāg bhavet
english: Nor should wealth be given to such men, by any means, while one has the power to refuse; for wealth given to the wicked torments even the giver. Therefore one who utters falsehood for the sake of dharma does not thereby become a liar.

sanskrit: eṣa te lakṣaṇoddeśaḥ samuddiṣṭo yathāvidhi etac chrutvā brūhi pārtha yadi vadhyo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: This summary of dharma's marks I have set forth for you according to rule. Having heard it, tell me, Pārtha: is Yudhiṣṭhira to be slain?

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca yathā brūyān mahāprājño yathā brūyān mahāmatiḥ hitaṃ caiva yathāsmākaṃ tathaitad vacanaṃ tava
english: Arjuna said: As a man of vast wisdom would speak, as one of great understanding would speak, and as is for our good — even so is this speech of yours.

sanskrit: bhavān mātṛsamo 'smākaṃ tathā pitṛsamo 'pi ca gatiś ca paramā kṛṣṇa tena te vākyam adbhutam
english: You are to us as a mother, and likewise as a father, and our supreme refuge, Kṛṣṇa; therefore your word is wondrous.

sanskrit: na hi te triṣu lokeṣu vidyate 'viditaṃ kva cit tasmād bhavān paraṃ dharmaṃ veda sarvaṃ yathātatham
english: For in the three worlds there is nothing anywhere unknown to you; therefore you know the highest dharma, all of it, exactly as it is.

sanskrit: avadhyaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ manye dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram tasmin samayasaṃyoge brūhi kiṃ cid anugraham idaṃ cāparam atraiva śṛṇu hṛtsthaṃ vivakṣitam
english: I hold the Pāṇḍava, Yudhiṣṭhira the Dharma-king, not to be slain. Within the bounds of that compact, speak some favor for him. And hear yet this other thing I would say, that lies within my heart.

sanskrit: jānāsi dāśārha mama vrataṃ tvaṃ; yo māṃ brūyāt kaś cana mānuṣeṣu anyasmai tvaṃ gāṇḍivaṃ dehi pārtha; yas tvatto 'strair bhavitā vā viśiṣṭaḥ
english: You know my vow, O Dāśārha: should any man among mortals say to me, 'Give over your Gāṇḍīva, Pārtha, to another,' or, 'There is one who surpasses you in arms' —

sanskrit: hanyām ahaṃ keśava taṃ prasahya; bhīmo hanyāt tūbaraketi coktaḥ tan me rājā proktavāṃs te samakṣaṃ; dhanur dehīty asakṛd vṛṣṇisiṃha
english: — him would I slay outright, Keśava; and one who calls me a beardless weakling, Bhīma would slay. Now this very thing the king said to me in your presence, lion of the Vṛṣṇis: 'Give up your bow,' again and again.

sanskrit: taṃ hatvā cet keśava jīvaloke; sthātā kālaṃ nāham apy alpamātram sā ca pratijñā mama lokaprabuddhā; bhavet satyā dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭha yathā jīvet pāṇḍavo 'haṃ ca kṛṣṇa; tathā buddhiṃ dātum adyārhasi tvam
english: If I slay him, Keśava, I will not remain even a moment longer in the world of the living. Yet that vow of mine, known throughout the world, must be made true, O foremost of the upholders of dharma. So devise it, Kṛṣṇa, that the Pāṇḍava may live and I as well — such counsel you must give me now.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca rājā śrānto jagato vikṣataś ca; karṇena saṃkhye niśitair bāṇasaṃghaiḥ tasmāt pārtha tvāṃ paruṣāṇy avocat; karṇe dyūtaṃ hy adya raṇe nibaddham
english: Vāsudeva said: The king is worn out and wounded, gashed by Karṇa in the fray with showers of whetted arrows. That is why, Pārtha, he spoke harshly to you; for upon Karṇa today the whole game of battle is staked.

sanskrit: tasmin hate kuravo nirjitāḥ syur; evaṃbuddhiḥ pārthivo dharmaputraḥ yadāvamānaṃ labhate mahāntaṃ; tadā jīvan mṛta ity ucyate saḥ
english: 'With him slain, the Kurus will be vanquished' — such is the mind of the king, the son of Dharma. When a man suffers a great humiliation, then, though he lives, he is called as good as dead.

sanskrit: tan mānitaḥ pārthivo 'yaṃ sadaiva; tvayā sabhīmena tathā yamābhyām vṛddhaiś ca loke puruṣapravīrais; tasyāvamānaṃ kalayā tvaṃ prayuṅkṣva
english: This king has ever been honored — by you, by Bhīma, and by the twins, and by elders and the foremost of men throughout the world. Therefore apply to him only a fraction of disrespect.

sanskrit: tvam ity atrabhavantaṃ tvaṃ brūhi pārtha yudhiṣṭhiram tvam ity ukto hi nihato gurur bhavati bhārata
english: Address this venerable one, Pārtha, with the familiar 'thou' — say 'thou' to Yudhiṣṭhira; for a guru addressed as 'thou' is thereby, as it were, slain, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: evam ācara kaunteya dharmarāje yudhiṣṭhire adharmayuktaṃ saṃyogaṃ kuruṣvaivaṃ kurūdvaha
english: So conduct yourself, son of Kuntī, toward the Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira; effect in this way a token of dishonor, O upholder of the Kurus.

sanskrit: atharvāṅgirasī hy eṣā śrutīnām uttamā śrutiḥ avicāryaiva kāryaiṣā śreyaḥkāmair naraiḥ sadā
english: For this is a teaching of the Atharvan and the Aṅgirasas, the highest of revealed teachings; and it is to be carried out without question, always, by men who desire their welfare.

sanskrit: vadho hy ayaṃ pāṇḍava dharmarājñas; tvatto yukto vetsyate caivam eṣaḥ tato 'sya pādāv abhivādya paścāc; chamaṃ brūyāḥ sāntvapūrvaṃ ca pārtham
english: For this, Pāṇḍava, will be reckoned a slaying of the Dharma-king at your hands; thus shall it be understood. And thereafter, having bowed to his feet and soothed him, you must speak peace, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: bhrātā prājñas tava kopaṃ na jātu; kuryād rājā kaṃ cana pāṇḍaveyaḥ mukto 'nṛtād bhrātṛvadhāc ca pārtha; hṛṣṭaḥ karṇaṃ tvaṃ jahi sūtaputram
english: Your wise brother, the king, the son of Pāṇḍu, will never harbor any anger against you. Freed of falsehood and of a brother's slaying, Pārtha, joyfully strike down Karṇa, the sūta's son.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ity evam uktas tu janārdanena; pārthaḥ praśasyātha suhṛdvadhaṃ tam tato 'bravīd arjuno dharmarājam; anuktapūrvaṃ paruṣaṃ prasahya
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed by Janārdana, Pārtha approved that 'slaying' of his dear one, and then Arjuna spoke to the Dharma-king, harshly and by force, words such as he had never uttered before.

sanskrit: mā tvaṃ rājan vyāhara vyāharatsu; na tiṣṭhase krośamātre raṇārdhe bhīmas tu mām arhati garhaṇāya; yo yudhyate sarvayodhapravīraḥ
english: Speak not, O king, while others speak; you do not even hold your ground within a krośa's distance of the battle's midst. It is Bhīma who has the right to reproach me — he who fights as the foremost champion of all warriors,

sanskrit: kāle hi śatrūn pratipīḍya saṃkhye; hatvā ca śūrān pṛthivīpatīṃs tān yaḥ kuñjarāṇām adhikaṃ sahasraṃ; hatvānadat tumulaṃ siṃhanādam
english: — who, in season pressing back the foe in battle and slaying those heroic lords of earth, having killed more than a thousand elephants, roared out his tumultuous lion's roar;

sanskrit: suduṣkaraṃ karma karoti vīraḥ; kartuṃ yathā nārhasi tvaṃ kadā cit rathād avaplutya gadāṃ parāmṛśaṃs; tayā nihanty aśvanaradvipān raṇe
english: That hero does deeds most hard to do, such as you could never do at any time: leaping down from his chariot and seizing his mace, with it he strikes down horses, men, and elephants in the fray.

sanskrit: varāsinā vājirathāśvakuñjarāṃs; tathā rathāṅgair dhanuṣā ca hanty arīn pramṛdya padbhyām ahitān nihanti yaḥ; punaś ca dorbhyāṃ śatamanyuvikramaḥ
english: With his fine sword he slays steeds, chariots, horses and elephants, and with chariot-wheels and bow he slays his foes; trampling his enemies underfoot he destroys them, and again with his two arms — he whose valor is that of Indra of the hundred sacrifices.

sanskrit: mahābalo vaiśravaṇāntakopamaḥ; prasahya hantā dviṣatāṃ yathārham sa bhīmaseno 'rhati garhaṇāṃ me; na tvaṃ nityaṃ rakṣyase yaḥ suhṛdbhiḥ
english: Of mighty strength, the equal of Kubera and of Yama, slayer by main force of his foes as they deserve — it is that Bhīmasena who has the right to reproach me, not you, who are forever guarded by your friends.

sanskrit: mahārathān nāgavarān hayāṃś ca; padātimukhyān api ca pramathya eko bhīmo dhārtarāṣṭreṣu magnaḥ; sa mām upālabdhum ariṃdamo 'rhati
english: Crushing great car-warriors, the noblest elephants, horses, and chief among the foot-soldiers, Bhīma alone has plunged into the host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons; it is that subduer of foes who has the right to rebuke me.

sanskrit: kaliṅgavaṅgāṅganiṣādamāgadhān; sadāmadān nīlabalāhakopamān nihanti yaḥ śatrugaṇān anekaśaḥ; sa mābhivaktuṃ prabhavaty anāgasam
english: He who slays in their multitudes the hosts of the Kaliṅgas, Vaṅgas, Aṅgas, Niṣādas, and Māgadhas — ever rut-maddened, like dark thunderclouds — he is able to upbraid me who am blameless.

sanskrit: suyuktam āsthāya rathaṃ hi kāle; dhanur vikarṣañ śarapūrṇamuṣṭiḥ sṛjaty asau śaravarṣāṇi vīro; mahāhave megha ivāmbudhārāḥ
english: Mounting in season his well-yoked car, drawing his bow, his fist full of arrows, that hero pours forth showers of shafts in the great battle, as a cloud pours forth its streams of water.

sanskrit: balaṃ tu vāci dvijasattamānāṃ; kṣātraṃ budhā bāhubalaṃ vadanti tvaṃ vāgbalo bhārata niṣṭhuraś ca; tvam eva māṃ vetsi yathāvidho 'ham
english: The wise say that the strength of the best of brahmins lies in speech, but the strength of the warrior in the might of his arms. You, Bhārata, are strong only in words, and harsh withal; you yourself know what manner of man I am.

sanskrit: yatāmi nityaṃ tava kartum iṣṭaṃ; dāraiḥ sutair jīvitenātmanā ca evaṃ ca māṃ vāgviśikhair nihaṃsi; tvattaḥ sukhaṃ na vayaṃ vidma kiṃ cit
english: I strive ever to do what is dear to you, with wife and sons and life and my own self; and yet you strike me down with the arrows of your speech. From you we have never known any happiness at all.

sanskrit: avāmaṃsthā māṃ draupadītalpasaṃstho; mahārathān pratihanmi tvadarthe tenātiśaṅkī bhārata niṣṭhuro 'si; tvattaḥ sukhaṃ nābhijānāmi kiṃ cit
english: You have despised me, you who keep to Draupadī's couch, while for your sake I slay great car-warriors; thus, over-suspicious, Bhārata, you are harsh. From you I have known no happiness whatever.

sanskrit: proktaḥ svayaṃ satyasaṃdhena mṛtyus; tava priyārthaṃ naradeva yuddhe vīraḥ śikhaṇḍī draupado 'sau mahātmā; mayābhiguptena hataś ca tena
english: By Bhīṣma, true to his word, the manner of his own death was himself declared; and for your pleasure, O lord of men, in battle the heroic Śikhaṇḍin, Drupada's great son, guarded by me, slew him.

sanskrit: na cābhinandāmi tavādhirājyaṃ; yatas tvam akṣeṣv ahitāya saktaḥ svayaṃ kṛtvā pāpam anāryajuṣṭam; ebhir yuddhe tartum icchasy arīṃs tu
english: Nor do I rejoice in your sovereignty, since you clung to the dice to our ruin; having yourself committed a sin practiced only by the ignoble, you now wish to cross over your foes in battle by means of these your brothers.

sanskrit: akṣeṣu doṣā bahavo vidharmāḥ; śrutās tvayā sahadevo 'bravīd yān tān naiṣi saṃtartum asādhujuṣṭān; yena sma sarve nirayaṃ prapannāḥ
english: Many are the faults of the dice, contrary to all law — those that Sahadeva named, you heard them. Yet you would not cross beyond those vices, fit only for the wicked, through which we have all gone down to hell.

sanskrit: tvaṃ devitā tvatkṛte rājyanāśas; tvat saṃbhavaṃ vyasanaṃ no narendra māsmān krūrair vākpratodais tuda tvaṃ; bhūyo rājan kopayann alpabhāgyān
english: You were the gambler; through you came the loss of the kingdom; from you arose our calamity, O lord of men. Goad us no more with the cruel whips of your words, O king, kindling the wrath of us ill-fated ones.

sanskrit: etā vācaḥ paruṣāḥ savyasācī; sthiraprajñaṃ śrāvayitvā tatakṣa tadānutepe surarājaputro; viniḥśvasaṃś cāpy asim udbabarha
english: Having made the steadfast-minded king hear these harsh words, Savyasācin cut him to the quick; then the son of the king of gods repented, and sighing deeply drew forth his sword.

sanskrit: tam āha kṛṣṇaḥ kim idaṃ punar bhavān; vikośam ākāśanibhaṃ karoty asim prabrūhi satyaṃ punar uttaraṃ vidher; vacaḥ pravakṣyāmy aham arthasiddhaye
english: Kṛṣṇa said to him: Why now do you draw from its sheath this sword, sky-bright? Tell me truly your answer again; then will I speak the word of counsel for the accomplishing of the end.

sanskrit: ity eva pṛṣṭaḥ puruṣottamena; suduḥkhitaḥ keśavam āha vākyam ahaṃ haniṣye svaśarīram eva; prasahya yenāhitam ācaraṃ vai
english: Thus questioned by that best of men, deeply grieved, Arjuna spoke to Keśava: I shall slay my own body by force — this body wherewith I have done so unfit a thing.

sanskrit: niśamya tat pārthavaco 'bravīd idaṃ; dhanaṃjayaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ prabrūhi pārtha svaguṇān ihātmanas; tathā svahārdaṃ bhavatīha sadyaḥ
english: Hearing that word of Pārtha, the foremost of the upholders of dharma said this to Dhanaṃjaya: Proclaim here your own virtues, Pārtha; thus at once will your heart's grief be lifted from you.

sanskrit: tathāstu kṛṣṇety abhinandya vākyaṃ; dhanaṃjayaḥ prāha dhanur vināmya yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaṃ; śṛṇuṣva rājann iti śakrasūnuḥ
english: 'So be it, Kṛṣṇa,' said Dhanaṃjaya, hailing the word, and lowering his bow he spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira, the foremost of the upholders of dharma — 'Hear me, O king,' said the son of Śakra:

sanskrit: na mādṛśo 'nyo naradeva vidyate; dhanurdharo devam ṛte pinākinam ahaṃ hi tenānumato mahātmanā; kṣaṇena hanyāṃ sacarācaraṃ jagat
english: There is no other bowman like me, O lord of men, save the god who bears the Pināka; for, sanctioned by that great one, in a moment I could destroy the world with all that moves and moves not.

sanskrit: mayā hi rājan sadigīśvarā diśo; vijitya sarvā bhavataḥ kṛtā vaśe sa rājasūyaś ca samāptadakṣiṇaḥ; sabhā ca divyā bhavato mamaujasā
english: For by me, O king, all the quarters, with the lords that rule them, were conquered and brought under your sway; that Rājasūya, with its gifts complete, and your celestial hall — these were yours through my might.

sanskrit: pāṇau pṛṣatkā likhitā mameme; dhanuś ca saṃkhye vitataṃ sabāṇam pādau ca me saśarau sahadhvajau; na mādṛśaṃ yuddhagataṃ jayanti
english: Upon my palm these shaft-marks are inscribed, and in battle my bow is drawn taut with its arrow; my feet too are marked with shafts and banner. One like me, gone to battle, none can conquer.

sanskrit: hatā udīcyā nihatāḥ pratīcyāḥ; prācyā nirastā dākṣiṇātyā viśastāḥ saṃśaptakānāṃ kiṃ cid evāvaśiṣṭaṃ; sarvasya sainyasya hataṃ mayārdham
english: The northern peoples are slain, the western struck down, the eastern routed, the southern destroyed; of the Saṃśaptakas but a remnant is left. Half of the entire host has been slain by me.

sanskrit: śete mayā nihatā bhāratī ca; camū rājan devacamūprakāśā ye nāstrajñās tān ahaṃ hanmi śastrais; tasmāl lokaṃ neha karomi bhasmasāt
english: The army of the Bhāratas, bright as the host of the gods, lies slain by me, O king. Those who know not the celestial weapons I slay with ordinary arms; therefore I do not reduce the world to ashes.

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā punar āha pārtho; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭham apy aputrā tena rādhā bhavitrī; kuntī mayā vā tad ṛtaṃ viddhi rājan prasīda rājan kṣama yan mayoktaṃ; kāle bhavān vetsyati tan namas te
english: Having spoken thus, Pārtha said again to Yudhiṣṭhira, the foremost of the upholders of dharma: By him shall Rādhā be made childless, or Kuntī by me — know this for the truth, O king. Be gracious, O king; forgive what I have spoken; in time you will understand it. To you my homage.

sanskrit: prasādya rājānam amitrasāhaṃ; sthito 'bravīc cainam abhiprapannaḥ yāmy eṣa bhīmaṃ samarāt pramoktuṃ; sarvātmanā sūtaputraṃ ca hantum
english: Having appeased the king, the conqueror of foes, he stood and, drawing near, said to him: I go now to deliver Bhīma from the fray, and with my whole soul to slay the sūta's son.

sanskrit: tava priyārthaṃ mama jīvitaṃ hi; bravīmi satyaṃ tad avehi rājan iti prāyād upasaṃgṛhya pādau; samutthito dīptatejāḥ kirīṭī nedaṃ cirāt kṣipram idaṃ bhaviṣyaty; āvartate 'sāv abhiyāmi cainam
english: For your pleasure is my very life — I speak the truth; know it so, O king. And so, having clasped his feet, the Diademed One of blazing splendor rose and set out: 'Soon, not long hence, this shall come to pass; yonder he turns — I go against him.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā pāṇḍavo dharmarājo; bhrātur vākyaṃ paruṣaṃ phalgunasya utthāya tasmāc chayanād uvāca; pārthaṃ tato duḥkhaparītacetāḥ
english: Hearing this, the Pāṇḍava, the Dharma-king, his brother Phalguna's harsh speech, rose from that couch and, his mind overwhelmed with grief, spoke then to Pārtha:

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ mayā pārtha yathā na sādhu; yena prāptaṃ vyasanaṃ vaḥ sughoram tasmāc chiraś chinddhi mamedam adya; kulāntakasyādhamapūruṣasya
english: I have acted, Pārtha, in a way that was not good, whereby this most dreadful calamity has come upon you all. Therefore strike off this head of mine today — the head of one who is the ruin of his line, the basest of men.

sanskrit: pāpasya pāpavyasanānvitasya; vimūḍhabuddher alasasya bhīroḥ vṛddhāvamantuḥ paruṣasya caiva; kiṃ te ciraṃ mām anuvṛtya rūkṣam
english: Of a sinner, beset with the vice of sin, of dull wit, slothful, and a coward, a scorner of his elders and a harsh man too — what use is it to you to follow me, a hard man, any longer?

sanskrit: gacchāmy ahaṃ vanam evādya pāpaḥ; sukhaṃ bhavān vartatāṃ madvihīnaḥ yogyo rājā bhīmaseno mahātmā; klībasya vā mama kiṃ rājyakṛtyam
english: I, a sinner, shall go this very day to the forest; may you live happily, rid of me. The great-souled Bhīmasena is fit to be king; what business has a eunuch like me with ruling?

sanskrit: na cāsmi śaktaḥ paruṣāṇi soḍhuṃ; punas tavemāni ruṣānvitasya bhīmo 'stu rājā mama jīvitena; kiṃ kāryam adyāvamatasya vīra
english: Nor am I able to bear these harsh words of yours again, spoken in anger. Let Bhīma be king; what use is there in my life, O hero, now that I am despised?

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā sahasotpapāta; rājā tatas tac chayanaṃ vihāya iyeṣa nirgantum atho vanāya; taṃ vāsudevaḥ praṇato 'bhyuvāca
english: Having spoken thus, the king sprang up at once, leaving that couch behind, and sought to go forth then to the forest; but Vāsudeva, bowing, said to him:

sanskrit: rājan viditam etat te yathā gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ pratijñā satyasaṃdhasya gāṇḍīvaṃ prati viśrutā
english: O king, this is known to you — how the vow of the Gāṇḍīva-bearer, faithful to his word, concerning the Gāṇḍīva is renowned far and wide.

sanskrit: brūyād ya evaṃ gāṇḍīvaṃ dehy anyasmai tvam ity uta sa vadhyo 'sya pumāṃl loke tvayā cokto 'yam īdṛśam
english: Whoever should say to him, 'Give over your Gāṇḍīva to another' — that man in the world is to be slain by him; and you spoke to him in just such terms.

sanskrit: ataḥ satyāṃ pratijñāṃ tāṃ pārthena parirakṣatā macchandād avamāno 'yaṃ kṛtas tava mahīpate gurūṇām avamāno hi vadha ity abhidhīyate
english: Therefore, to keep that vow of his true, Pārtha, at my urging, has shown you this disrespect, O lord of earth; for disrespect toward elders is called a slaying.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvaṃ vai mahābāho mama pārthasya cobhayoḥ vyatikramam imaṃ rājan saṃkṣamasvārjunaṃ prati
english: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, this transgression of us both — of me and of Pārtha — forgive it, O king, with regard to Arjuna.

sanskrit: śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ mahārāja prapannau sva ubhāv api kṣantum arhasi me rājan praṇatasyābhiyācataḥ
english: To you, great king, we have both come for refuge; you should forgive me, O king, as I bow and entreat you.

sanskrit: rādheyasyādya pāpasya bhūmiḥ pāsyati śoṇitam satyaṃ te pratijānāmi hataṃ viddhy adya sūtajam yasyecchasi vadhaṃ tasya gatam evādya jīvitam
english: This day the earth shall drink the blood of the wicked son of Rādhā; truly I promise you — know the sūta's son as slain today. He whose death you desire — his life is already gone this day.

sanskrit: iti kṛṣṇavacaḥ śrutvā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sasaṃbhramaṃ hṛṣīkeśam utthāpya praṇataṃ tadā kṛtāñjalim idaṃ vākyam uvācānantaraṃ vacaḥ
english: Hearing these words of Kṛṣṇa, the Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira hastily raised up Hṛṣīkeśa, who bowed before him, and then, with palms joined, spoke this word in answer:

sanskrit: evam etad yathāttha tvam asty eṣo 'tikramo mama anunīto 'smi govinda tāritaś cādya mādhava mokṣitā vyasanād ghorād vayam adya tvayācyuta
english: It is even as you say; this transgression is indeed mine. I am won over, Govinda, and delivered this day, Mādhava; rescued from dread calamity are we this day by you, O Acyuta.

sanskrit: bhavantaṃ nātham āsādya āvāṃ vyasanasāgarāt ghorād adya samuttīrṇāv ubhāv ajñānamohitau
english: Having gained you as our protector, we two, bewildered by ignorance, have this day crossed over from the dreadful ocean of calamity.

sanskrit: tvadbuddhiplavam āsādya duḥkhaśokārṇavād vayam samuttīrṇāḥ sahāmātyāḥ sanāthāḥ sma tvayācyuta
english: Boarding the raft of your wisdom, we, together with our counselors, have crossed over from the ocean of grief and sorrow; protected by you we are, O Acyuta.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca iti sma kṛṣṇavacanāt pratyuccārya yudhiṣṭhiram babhūva vimanāḥ pārthaḥ kiṃ cit kṛtveva pātakam
english: Saṃjaya said: Having thus, at Kṛṣṇa's word, retorted to Yudhiṣṭhira, Pārtha grew downcast, as though he had committed some sin.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd vāsudevaḥ prahasann iva pāṇḍavam kathaṃ nāma bhaved etad yadi tvaṃ pārtha dharmajam asinā tīkṣṇadhāreṇa hanyā dharme vyavasthitam
english: Then Vāsudeva, as if smiling, said to the Pāṇḍava: How indeed could this have come to pass, Pārtha — that you should slay with a keen-edged sword the son of Dharma, who stands firm in dharma?

sanskrit: tvam ity uktvaiva rājānam evaṃ kaśmalam āviśaḥ hatvā tu nṛpatiṃ pārtha akariṣyaḥ kim uttaram evaṃ sudurvido dharmo mandaprajñair viśeṣataḥ
english: Merely by saying 'thou' to the king you fell into such despondency; but had you slain the king, Pārtha, what answer could you have made? So very hard is dharma to discern, especially by those of feeble understanding.

sanskrit: sa bhavān dharmabhīrutvād dhruvam aiṣyan mahattamaṃ narakaṃ ghorarūpaṃ ca bhrātur jyeṣṭhasya vai vadhāt
english: You, from your dread of unrighteousness, would surely have gone to the most dreadful and terrible hell, for the slaying of your eldest brother.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ rājānaṃ dharmasaṃhitam prasādaya kuruśreṣṭham etad atra mataṃ mama
english: Therefore do you appease the king, the best of the upholders of dharma, joined to dharma, the foremost of the Kurus; this is my counsel herein.

sanskrit: prasādya bhaktyā rājānaṃ prītaṃ caiva yudhiṣṭhiram prayāmas tvaritā yoddhuṃ sūtaputrarathaṃ prati
english: Having appeased the king with devotion, and Yudhiṣṭhira being made glad, let us go in haste to fight against the chariot of the sūta's son.

sanskrit: hatvā sudurjayaṃ karṇaṃ tvam adya niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vipulāṃ prītim ādhatsva dharmaputrasya mānada
english: Slaying the hard-to-conquer Karṇa today with your whetted shafts, bring abundant joy to the son of Dharma, O giver of honor.

sanskrit: etad atra mahābāho prāptakālaṃ mataṃ mama evaṃ kṛte kṛtaṃ caiva tava kāryaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: This, O mighty-armed one, is my counsel, fitting to the hour; and when this is done, your task too will be accomplished.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno mahārāja lajjayā vai samanvitaḥ dharmarājasya caraṇau prapede śirasānagha
english: Then Arjuna, O great king, filled with shame, fell with his head at the feet of the Dharma-king, O sinless one.

sanskrit: uvāca bharataśreṣṭha prasīdeti punaḥ punaḥ kṣamasva rājan yat proktaṃ dharmakāmena bhīruṇā
english: He said, O best of the Bharatas: 'Be gracious,' again and again; 'forgive, O king, what was spoken by one who loves dharma and is fearful of it.'

sanskrit: pādayoḥ patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dhanaṃjayam amitraghnaṃ rudantaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Seeing Dhanaṃjaya, the slayer of foes, fallen at his feet and weeping, O bull of the Bharatas, the Dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira —

sanskrit: utthāpya bhrātaraṃ rājā dharmarājo dhanaṃjayam samāśliṣya ca sasnehaṃ praruroda mahīpatiḥ
english: — the king, the Dharma-king, raised up his brother Dhanaṃjaya and, embracing him with affection, the lord of earth burst into tears.

sanskrit: ruditvā tu ciraṃ kālaṃ bhrātarau sumahādyutī kṛtaśaucau naravyāghrau prītimantau babhūvatuḥ
english: Having wept for a long while, the two brothers of great splendor, those tigers among men, their hearts unburdened, became filled with mutual love.
